text:
Cristiano Ronaldo spent three seasons at Juventus, working under three different coaches and scoring many goals, but he was also a massive financial burden for the Old Lady; so how should we judge his time at the club?
When the Portuguese superstar moved to Turin in the summer of 2018, very few fans and pundits could believe their eyes.
The deal with Real Madrid cost the Bianconeri about €115m, and buying the best player in the world at the time was meant to give the Serie A giants a decisive boost in their desperate chase for the Champions League.
Over the previous campaigns, the Bianconeri had reached the Champions League Final twice, first in 2015 and then in 2017, losing this second one 4-1 in Cardiff to Ronaldo’s Real Madrid.
The Portuguese’s move to Juventus was initially a win for the club. Ronaldo scored his first goal with the Old Lady in his fourth competitive appearance, the second at home.
His arrival helped Juventus expand their global brand, attract millions of new fans worldwide and significantly grow their Instagram following through unmatched popularity and social media influence.
Ronaldo went on to score 101 goals in 134 appearances across all competitions for the Serie A giants in three years. During his time at the club, Juventus won several domestic trophies, including two Serie A titles, but didn’t get to win the coveted Champions League.
Issues began with the COVID pandemic, which hit every football club worldwide, but particularly Juventus. At the time, Ronaldo was in his second season at the club and was its highest-paid player, earning a €30m net salary.
Because of the COVID pandemic, Juventus made salary agreements with most of their players, including Ronaldo. But when he returned to Manchester United in 2021, he was still owed several months’ wages, sparking an ongoing legal battle.
Juventus’ domination of Italian football continued during Ronaldo’s first two years at the club, but during his final campaign, under Andrea Pirlo, the Bianconeri ended their nine-season winning streak, leaving the Serie A throne to Antonio Conte’s Inter in 2020-21.
Juventus’ domestic supremacy was so vast that it’s fair to imagine the club would still have won at least the first Scudetto in the Ronaldo era, but the Portuguese played a vital role in his second season under Maurizio Sarri, scoring 31 goals in 33 league games.
In the following campaign, he became Serie A’s top scorer with 29 goals, but Juventus qualified for the Champions League only on the final matchday.
On the field, Ronaldo helped Juventus achieve some of their main targets, but not the biggest one, the Champions League, while the financial burden he brought was further deepened by the COVID pandemic, during which Juventus not only had their highest-ever wage bill, but also couldn’t make the most of the Ronaldo effect due to games being played behind closed doors.
Although his three years at Juventus were hugely exciting for most Juventus fans worldwide, the club didn’t achieve the sporting and financial targets they had in mind when they signed him in 2018.
digest_he:
כריסטיאנו רונאלדו שיחק במשך שלוש עונות ביובנטוס תחת שלושה מאמנים שונים וכבש 101 שערים ב-134 הופעות בכל המסגרות. הגעתו ב-2018 תרמה להתרחבות המותג הגלובלי של המועדון, אך הוא גם היווה נטל כלכלי עצום, במיוחד בתקופת מגפת הקורונה שבה השתכר משכורת עתק בזמן שהמשחקים נערכו דלתיים סגורות.

בעוד שרונאלדו זכה בתארים מקומיים כולל שתי אליפויות סרייה א, הוא לא הצליח להביא ליובנטוס את ליגת האלופות, המטרה המרכזית לשמה הוחתם. בסופו של דבר, הקבוצה לא השיגה את היעדים הספורטיביים והפיננסיים שלה, והפורטוגלי עזב את איטליה ב-2021 בדרך חזרה למנצ'סטר יונייטד תוך כדי הותרת סוגיות משפטיות פתוחות.
